rules.notes: EQL Tools' naked cap is player-reported; not applied

rules.title: Natural Durability: percent of the HP that comes from STA, by rank

source.ref: eqlwiki AA data, revision 151303, as extracted by eqlbuilds.com

rules.notes: AA 107, type 4 in the client's text: increases your maximum base health (derived from your stamina) by #1%. The ranks (2, 5, 10 and 12 percent, costs 2, 4, 6 and 2) are the wiki's data. It scales only the HP that comes from STA (the hp_fac x STA' of 5 + base_hp + hp_fac x STA'), not the constant, the class base or the flat HP of items and buffs. The model assumes the top rank for every class, as it assumes Combat Stability 3 of 3; the window floors the STA part first and the scaled part after.

WIS multiplier bands for mana
rules.notes: Settled by an in-game stat window reading with no buffs: above the second break the slope stays the same up to the hard cap, with no bend at the stat knee. The flatter slope above the second break that the EQEmu code and a public stat page suggested is ruled out.

Stamina knee (into hit points)

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: The only break at 255 in the client is the one of stamina into hit points: above it a point of stamina counts half (hp.sta_curve). Strength, agility, wisdom, intelligence, charisma and dexterity have no break at 255: each counts in full up to the cap of 510 (wisdom and intelligence reach mana through the bands of mana.wis_bands, and the endurance average through its own breaks at 100 and 200).

rules.title: DEX benefit slope past 255

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: Dexterity has no break at 255 in the client: it counts in full up to the cap of 510, in the endurance average and, for a bow or a thrown weapon, in the attack. What the game server does with it (weapon procs) is not known.

rules.title: Haste cap
rules.value: max(level, 30) + 25 up to level 50 (75 at level 50), 85 for levels 51 to 59, 100 from level 60

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: The cap of the total haste (a haste spell, the best worn haste item and the other sources together) grows with the level to the value the game shows at the level cap of today, and rises in steps after it. Overhaste, which Unbound Alacrity is taken to be, lifts the cap by its own amount.

rules.title: Haste cap with a Monk in the trio
rules.value: the cap of the level plus the 10 that Unbound Alacrity adds (85 at level 50)

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.title: Unbound Alacrity: effect on haste
rules.value: adds 10 haste and raises the cap by 10

source.ref: patch notes 2026-07-28, Unbound Alacrity ("increase in your current and maximum haste value")

rules.notes: A trio with a Monk gets 10 haste that stacks with the best spell haste and the best worn haste, up to haste.cap_pct_with_monk (the cap already includes its 10). The wiki's Haste Guide says it grants up to 10% haste and raises the cap by 10%; the patch notes say it raises both the current and the maximum haste value. 2026-10-22: the weapon index is paid the haste the kit counts (the spell haste of the buffs it takes, this 10 included, plus the best worn haste it wears, up to the cap), not a haste the scenario could reach; the solver chooses the buffs and the haste item together with the weapons.

rules.title: A haste spell is assumed when a kit is chosen
rules.notes: A judgment, not a measurement. A trio may or may not have a hasting class awake, so with false a kit is chosen on gear haste alone: the haste of a spell is left out of the profile (the spell haste of the profile is the Monk's flat haste alone) and a worn haste item is then worth its full value, up to the cap. With true the haste of the buffs enters the profile as it did before, and the kit is chosen as if the best haste spell were always on. A reader who does have a haste spell ticks the box "I have a haste spell" under Buffs on a trio page: the kit is then worked out in the browser with the buff set that keeps the haste of the spells (a twin of each buff set in the bundle), which is what the rule true gives.

rules.title: Regen caps from gear
rules.notes: Player-reported; not measured.

rules.title: Resist cap

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: The cap of each resist in the client's stat window is 1000 up to level 65 (a level above 65 has (level + 135) x 5), and abilities of the Discordant Defiance kind raise it. The model valued the gear and buff resists of a school up to 200, a judgment, before.

rules.title: Tier stat rule

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: The client's own calculation agrees at whole tiers: a stat gains the larger of a point and a tenth of its base for each tier, truncated. The attack of an item is not one of the stats it scales (tier.unscaled_stats).

rules.title: Stats the tier rule leaves alone

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: Item attack never grows with the tier: a +4 or a +10 item's attack is its +0 value. The client's calculation leaves the heal amount, the spell damage, the clairvoyance and the delay alone too; the model carries attack only.

rules.title: Weight reduction per tier
rules.unit: percent of the base weight per tier
rules.notes: In tenths of a stone, the weight w at tier n becomes the larger of the floor and w minus nine percent of w for each tier (the amount taken off rounded down), with no minimum step. Weights read in game on several items fit it. Progress toward the next tier lowers the weight further in proportion, so an item part of the way to its next tier weighs less than it does at its tier; the site shows every item exactly at a tier. The floor is tier.weight_floor. The rounding of the last tenth of a stone is not settled.

rules.title: Weapon damage per tier
rules.notes: Damage at tier n is dmg + dmg*n*10//100 with no minimum of 1 a tier. Player client reads: a weapon of base damage 6 reads 8 at +4 and 9 at +5. Delay and the listed damage bonus do not change. The in-game test B5 can still confirm it; the robustness runs try the alternative.

rules.title: Tier at which each socket opens
Tier at which items arrive, by source

source.ref: developer hotfix notes 2026-07-29 and developer stream 2026-06-10

rules.title: Highest tier of a fresh drop
rules.notes: No fresh drop above this tier has been seen.

rules.title: Void-touched mote
rules.notes: A void-touched mote raises any one item by one whole tier, at any tier, up to the top tier, with no limit on the motes one item takes. Read in game. The order in which the site spends motes is greedy: each step is the mote, or the shortest run of motes on one item that gains anything, that adds the most kit value per mote to the kit as it stands.

rules.title: Negative stats shrink with tier
rules.value: toward zero by max(n, floor(|base|*n/10)), never past zero

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: A negative stat moves toward zero by the amount that a positive stat of the same size would grow, and never passes zero: a small negative stat is gone after a tier or two, and the resist or attribute of an item that is mostly a cost shrinks as the item is upgraded.

rules.title: Monk worn-weight bonus curve
rules.notes: EQL Tools' threshold of about 34 read as the end of the bonus

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

alternatives.value: on top of the capped sheet AC (bypasses the softcap), valued per sheet point

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.title: Berserker stance: swing speed, and agility
rules.unit: swing speed factor, agility in mitigation and evasion, and the builds that play the stance

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: While the Berserker stance is on, the swing timer is divided by the factor after the haste cap, so worn haste keeps its full value with or without a haste spell, and agility adds nothing to mitigation or to evasion. The model plays the stance for the builds listed (the Melee damage build) of a trio that has a Berserker; the other builds are taken to play another stance. The stance needs endurance above one percent, which the model takes to be kept up. The factor multiplies the swing of both hands and not a bow, and not a weapon proc (a proc is paced by the minute).

rules.title: Build weight templates
rules.notes: A judgment, not a measurement: every number here is a weight TrioForge chose, in hit-point equivalents for one point of the stat, and a reader can change them with Your priorities. A build is a way a trio plays, and each has its own weights. Tank: in front, in a Defensive stance, armour class first, then hit points and endurance, attack (2.67 a point, the weight its weapon's damage is scored with), a little mana, a worn haste item and the weapon at a factor of 0.5 (450 x 2.67 x 0.5 = 600.75 for a point of weapon damage index, against 1800 for Melee damage: a third of its weight). Shield caster: a tank class that does its damage with spells, so a shield and armour class first, then resists and hit points, and mana only a little (0.3 a point: a knight with two casters beside it has mana to spare, and gears for armour and resists); the weapon is a carrier of stats and counts no damage, and haste is not scored. Melee damage: attack, strength, dexterity and haste, then hit points; armour class and mana are small. Caster tank: no tank class, so armour class (a shield where a class can hold one), mana as a second health bar, hit points and resists; the weapon counts no damage. Caster: mana first, then hit points and resists; the weapon counts no damage. The Archer build is the Melee build with the factors of the rule Ranged role weight factors. The weight of weapon damage in each build is the rule Weapon damage weight times the build's attack weight times the rule Weapon damage factor of each build.

rules.title: Ranged role weight factors
rules.unit: multiplier on the Melee template's weight of that stat
rules.notes: A judgment, not a measurement. The Archer build is the Melee damage template (the rule Build weight templates, whatever it is now, so a change to Melee damage carries over) with the dexterity weight doubled and the armor class weight halved, for a Ranger who shoots from a distance and so is hit less: damage from a bow first (attack, dexterity and haste), then hit points. The other builds are not changed.

rules.title: Weapon damage factor of each build
rules.unit: multiplier on the weapon damage weight of the build
rules.notes: A judgment, not a measurement. How much the damage of the weapons counts in each build, as a multiplier on the weight the rule Weapon damage weight gives (that weight, times the build's attack weight, times this factor, is what a point of weapon damage index is worth). Melee damage and the Archer count the weapon in full; the Tank counts it at a factor of 0.5 (its weight is then 450 x 2.67 x 0.5 = 600.75 a point, against 1800 for Melee damage), so that a shield can win the off hand where the armour class it gives is worth more than a second weapon; the Shield caster, the Caster tank and the Caster count no weapon damage at all, so their weapons are chosen for stats. Your priorities scale it with attack, as before. One mechanism for every build: the earlier rule that only the Tank, Melee and Ranged templates scored damage is this table with a 0 for the others.

rules.title: Main-hand damage bonus when the item lists none
rules.unit: the level from which a main hand has the bonus, the factor of a one-hander and of a two-hander, and the most delay that counts

source.ref: EverQuest Legends client, build of 2026-11-17: the client's own calculation

rules.notes: bonus = (level / 100) x max(damage, level) x factor x min(delay, 50) / 40, from level 28 on, for the main hand of an item that lists no bonus (a listed bonus counts as it is, and a listed zero counts as none). At level 50, for a weapon whose damage is at most 50, this is half the delay for a one-hander and 0.6875 x min(delay, 50) for a two-hander. The client rounds the bonus down to a whole number when it shows it; the model keeps the exact value, as it always did. The off hand has no bonus.

rules.title: Weapon damage weight
rules.unit: HP-equivalents per damage-index point per unit of the build's ATK weight and of its weapon damage factor
rules.notes: A judgment. Multiplied by each build's attack weight and then by the rule Weapon damage factor of each build. 2026-11-19: 600 became 450 when the attack weight of Melee damage rose from 3 to 4, so that the weapon weight of Melee damage stays at 1800 (a third more attack weight, a quarter less per point). One ATK point is taken as worth about a tenth of a percent of melee damage.

rules.title: Dual-wield off-hand factor
rules.unit: fraction, by whether the trio has a Monk
rules.notes: The share of the off hand's damage that counts in the weapon index. Derivation: min(1, best Dual Wield skill / 400 x 1.32), with the Dual Wield skill at 252 for a Monk and 210 for the other dual wielders, and Ambidexterity as the x1.32: 0.83 with a Monk in the trio, 0.69 without. The source calls this a working model, not a measured figure, so the rule stays open.

rules.title: Bow damage factor
rules.unit: multiplier on the weapon damage index of a bow in the range place
rules.notes: A judgment, not a measurement. In the Bow setup the bow in the range place is scored on its own damage per delay, at the haste the kit counts (its damage over its delay, times one plus the haste), times this number. 1 says a bow shot counts as much as the swing of a main hand with the same damage and delay, before that main hand's bonus. The damage bonus of a main hand is not counted for a bow: nothing in the game data says that archery gets it, and no bow lists one. Arrow damage is not counted, and nothing else about shooting is.

rules.title: Races counted as close for the default race
rules.notes: A judgment, not a measurement. Only races that can be created at character creation take part. Races whose value in the opening view is within this percent of the best of them are close: the window is measured from the best race that can be created, not from the best race overall, so a race that cannot be created never sets it and is never named. The data lists the close races in order of value, the default race first (a tie goes in the display order of the races), and is empty when the best creatable race stands alone or its value is not above 0; the page says close instead of naming a best race. The default race is the best race that can be created.

rules.title: Value of one percent of each kind of focus
rules.unit: relative to one percent of damage or healing
rules.notes: How much a focus kind is worth next to damage; used to rank the foci of the Effects to exalt section.

rules.title: How much a class leans on each kind of spell
rules.notes: Weights how much of a class's late spells a focus touches. A kind that is not listed (utility, summoned items, teleports, illusions) counts as the weight of other.

rules.title: Kinds of spell that make a class a caster in a fight
rules.notes: A class's cast mass is the weight of its late spells of these kinds.

rules.title: Weight of late combat spells that counts as a full caster
rules.notes: A class with this weight of late spells of the kinds above, or more, has cast mass 1.

rules.title: First spell level that counts as late
rules.notes: A level-50 character still casts spells from this level up.

rules.title: Relevance of a click or worn effect to each role
rules.unit: relevance, 0 to 1, for a tank, a melee and a caster role
rules.notes: Dispel has a rule of its own (effects.dispel_relevance).

rules.title: Relevance of a dispel click to each role
rules.unit: relevance, 0 to 1, for a tank, a melee and a caster role
rules.notes: The site's default is difficulty 4 content, where mobs carry buffs, so a click that strips four of them (Pillage Enchantment) is worth more than the trio's own one-buff dispel spell. It is a constant, not a difficulty switch. A dispel is scored by how many buffs it strips, and no cut applies for the trio's own Cancel Magic: the click is free and instant.

rules.title: Kinds of click that only fill a gap
rules.notes: Cut to a fraction when a trio class already has its own spell of the kind up to the cap.

rules.title: Kinds of click compared with the trio's own best spell
rules.notes: The magnitude of the click is compared with the trio's own best spell of the same kind.

rules.title: Kinds of click that gain from being instant
rules.notes: An instant click skips spell recovery, which a caster values.

rules.title: Bonus of an instant output click for a caster
rules.unit: fraction of the score, times the role's spell factor
rules.notes: Applied to the kinds in effects.instant_categories.

rules.title: Value of one proc, by kind, next to damage
rules.unit: fraction of a full damage proc
rules.notes: A proc of a kind that is not listed counts for the unlisted_proc factor of effects.score_shape. Damage procs are scaled by their size against the strong ones.

rules.title: Constants of the click, proc and role scores
rules.notes: gap_utility scales a utility click below an output click; gap_covered is the cut for a gap already covered by the trio's own spell; no_magnitude is the size taken for a click with no number; own_floor and own_span give the part of an output click's score that depends on beating the trio's own spell; proc_melee_floor is the least share of melee classes counted for a proc and proc_full_percentile the proc damage percentile that counts as a full score; spell_floor and spell_span make the spell factor of a role from its mana weight; off_role_class is the weight of a class outside the role's group.

rules.title: Haste buff classes, and what a haste click or proc is worth next to them
rules.notes: A trio class with a haste buff of min_pct or more for a player (not pet-only) cuts a haste click or proc to the cut factor. Beastlord is counted by decision although its only haste spell targets the pet. Worn haste is an item stat and is never moved.

rules.title: Share of the best focus score within which the cheapest source wins
rules.notes: Among the donors of a focus type within this share of the best score, the easiest to get wins.

rules.title: Cost of getting an item, by source
rules.notes: Vendor, quest or crafted, drop in a group zone, drop in a raid zone, no known source.

rules.title: Zones that need a raid or a hard group
rules.notes: Level cap 50 content. A zone whose name starts with Plane of counts too.

rules.title: Effect ids of odd one-off utility spells
rules.notes: Size change, identify, locate corpse, telescope and the like are grouped as other utility.

rules.title: Damage that only works on some targets
rules.unit: spell target types, fraction of plain damage
rules.notes: Dismiss and Banish spells (animals, undead, summoned) are scored at this fraction of a plain damage spell of their size.

rules.title: Effects whose description may differ from the spell data
rules.notes: Marked unverified on the page. The spell data says a small damage proc with a stun; players call it a hate proc.

rules.title: Rows of each list kept for a trio
rules.notes: The best rows of each kind, which the page shows and the placement on a kit uses.

rules.title: Procs a minute of a weapon
rules.unit: procs a minute = (DEX / dex_divisor + base) x (1 + rate / 100), the rate being the Rate line of the item's effect (0 when it lists none)
rules.notes: A judgment fitted to rates measured in play at a DEX of roughly 200 to 255; how the rate depends on DEX is not measured, which is why the DEX it is evaluated at is one fixed number (effects.proc_reference_dex) and not the DEX of the kit. Procs are paced by the minute and not by the swing, so the rate does not grow with haste, and the proc of a weapon has no haste factor in the weapon term. The Rate line is the modifier and is applied here, once, and nowhere else. The weapon term counts one proc for each hand that swings: the better of the item's own proc and the best proc it can host once an item is at the tier where the proc socket opens (a maximum, never a sum; whether a native proc and a socketed one both fire is not known), and the off hand counts it by the dual-wield factor (weapons.dual_wield_factor, a judgment: how the off hand paces a proc is not measured). A proc is worth the weapon weight of the build, so it counts as much as the same damage a second from a swing.

rules.title: The DEX at which the proc rate is evaluated
rules.notes: A judgment: one fixed DEX for every scenario, so that the weapon term stays a sum of terms of the items worn and the solve stays exact. It sits inside the range the rate of procs a minute was fitted at.

rules.title: Share of procs that land
rules.unit: fraction of the damage-equivalent of a proc
rules.notes: A judgment: some procs are resisted. It multiplies the size of every kind of proc, a damage proc and the others alike.

rules.title: A proc of a kind the trio casts itself
rules.unit: factor on the size of a proc that is not damage
rules.notes: A judgment, the cut a utility click gets when the trio's own spell covers the gap (effects.score_shape gap_covered). A proc that is not damage (a slow, a stun, a debuff) counts this fraction of its size when a class of the trio has a spell of the same kind at least as strong. A haste proc keeps the cut of effects.haste_buff instead.

rules.title: Which unverified procs count in the weapon term
rules.notes: A judgment. A proc record with no mark counts in full. One marked ambiguous (its name matches several spells of the client's text) counts at the smaller of its candidate spells. A mark that is not listed counts nothing: inferred (a proc inferred from a weapon whose page has no trigger wording) and description (players describe the effect differently from the spell data). Such records stay in the lists of effects to exalt.
